definition: Assigning semantic labels to every point or voxel in a 3D scene, extending 2D segmentation to LiDAR and RGB-D data.
details: Assigning semantic labels to every point or voxel in a 3D scene, extending 2D segmentation to LiDAR and RGB-D data.

explainer.lead: 3D semantic segmentation gives every point or small volume in a three-dimensional scene a meaning, such as road, car, or wall. It turns raw LiDAR or RGB-D measurements into a labeled scene that other systems can reason about.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a 3D picture made of tiny dots or building blocks, and you color each one by what it belongs to: blue for road, red for cars, and green for trees. The computer is doing that coloring for the whole scene, not just drawing a box around an object.
tiers.practitioner: A model consumes a LiDAR point cloud or RGB-D scene and predicts one semantic class per point or voxel, using either point-based or voxel-based representations. Useful checks include whether labels remain aligned with the original coordinates and whether predictions are evaluated per point or per voxel, since the representations differ.
tiers.paperLevel: Given a 3D scene S represented as points P = {p_1, ..., p_n} or voxels V, learn a mapping f such that f(p_i) = c_i or f(v_j) = c_j, where each c belongs to a fixed semantic label set C. The output therefore assigns a class to every input element rather than only detecting or classifying whole objects.

explainer.example: For a LiDAR scan beside a road, the model labels ground points as road, points on a nearby car as vehicle, points on a person as pedestrian, and points on trunks and leaves as vegetation. Every point receives one of these labels, producing a semantic 3D map of the scan.

usedIn.name: Autonomous driving
usedIn.detail: LiDAR scenes can be labeled into categories such as road, vehicles, and pedestrians.

usedIn.name: Robotics
usedIn.detail: Labeled 3D surroundings can distinguish surfaces and objects in a robot's environment.

usedIn.name: Indoor scene understanding
usedIn.detail: RGB-D data can be segmented into semantic regions such as walls, floors, and furniture.

explainer.intuition: Instead of asking only what appears in a scene, the task asks what every small piece of the scene is. The result is a dense 3D label map aligned with the points or voxels.
howItWorks: Capture a 3D scene as LiDAR points or RGB-D measurements.
Represent the scene as individual points or divide it into voxels.
Use a model to predict a semantic class for each point or voxel.
Combine the predictions into a fully labeled 3D scene.
explainer.whyItMatters: It provides fine-grained scene structure in three dimensions, preserving where each semantic region is rather than reducing the scene to object boxes or a single category. This makes LiDAR and RGB-D data easier for downstream systems to interpret.
misconceptions: It is not the same as 3D object detection: detection locates objects, while semantic segmentation labels every point or voxel.
It does not necessarily separate individual objects: two cars can both receive the vehicle label without receiving different instance identities.
